verified.name: Engine Ventures
verified.thesis: Engine Ventures invests in early-stage Tough Tech founders by providing capital, operational expertise, and a powerful academic, commercial, and governmental network to build and scale companies unlocking massive opportunities in foundational industries. The firm backs companies rebuilding the systems the world depends on by solving difficult problems across energy, materials, infrastructure, computing, human health, and related sectors.
verified.notes: Engine Ventures is the rebranded venture capital entity that separated from The Engine nonprofit incubator in 2023. The Engine nonprofit (founded 2016) continues to operate as a separate 501(c)(3) organization. Katie Rae is CEO & Managing Partner; Israel Ruiz is President & General Partner.

changesProposed.name: General Catalyst

verified.name: General Catalyst
verified.thesis: General Catalyst invests across seed, venture, and growth stages. The firm focuses on applying AI to transform critical institutions, particularly in healthcare and defense.
verified.notes: In June 2024, General Catalyst acquired La Famiglia (German VC firm) and Venture Highway (India-based early-stage investor). In December 2025, agreed to acquire Janus Henderson for approximately $7.4 billion (increased to $8 billion in March 2026). In May 2025, launched £30 million medical technology venture fund with UK NHS and Speedinvest. Founded by Joel Cutler and David Fialkow in 2000.

changesProposed.name: Y Combinator

verified.name: Y Combinator
verified.thesis: Y Combinator invests $500,000 per company ($125,000 for 7% equity on post-money SAFE and $375,000 on uncapped SAFE with MFN clause) in startups accepted into four annual batches. Companies move to San Francisco for three months of intensive mentorship, office hours, and community support, culminating in Demo Day presentation to investors. Y Combinator and its alumni network continue supporting founders beyond the initial program.
verified.notes: Garry Tan became President and CEO in January 2023. Headquarters moved from Mountain View to San Francisco in spring 2023. YC has funded over 5,000 companies with over 100 unicorns.
